screens.title: Why the form must read Global.cs as it opens
screens.goal: Each time the data entry form opens it is brand new and empty, but Global.cs still holds everything.

blocks.p: The Take quiz button closes the data entry form. The Return button on the quiz opens a new one.

drawn.alt: A brand new empty data entry form on the left. Global.cs on the right still holds the quiz score.
drawn.say: The new data entry form is empty. Global.cs still holds everything.

blocks.p: Every time the data entry form opens, it is brand new. Nothing typed before is in it.
Global.cs still has it all. So the form must ask Global.cs, the moment it opens.
Code that runs the moment a form opens is a Load event. You met one in chapter 7.

screens.title: Plan the Load event and make it
screens.goal: The Load event switches every panel off, asks Global.cs three questions, then fills the boxes and switches on the right panel.

blocks.p: The Load event does three jobs, in this order.
First, it switches all five panels off. Second, it asks Global.cs three questions.
Third, from the answers, it fills the boxes and switches on the right panel.

steps.do: In Solution Explorer, double-click frmDataEntry. It opens in the Design tab.
steps.see: You can see the data entry form with its panels.

steps.do: Double-click the form's title bar at the top of the form.
steps.see: The code tab opens. Visual Studio has written frmDataEntry_Load for you.

Hide it. It is still there, but nobody can see it.
blocks.intro: Two new things in this chapter. Click any marked word to see what it means.

blocks.p: [[ForeColor|0]] is the colour of the writing. [[Visible = false|1]] hides the Take quiz button.

blocks.p: Question 2 for Global.cs: has the average been worked out? If yes, put the numbers back.
The numbers are kept as numbers. .ToString() turns each one into words for its box.
